_about: Infrastructure (netblock and autonomous-system) correlation signals: the evidence that ties a netblock or an AS to a target organization, so an enumeration's scope can be made more complete. docs/ai/INFRASTRUCTURE.md and `amass review infrastructure-signals` are generated from this file; edit the rationale here. Each signal's weight times 100 is the confidence the related-infrastructure lens records for an asset the signal supports; an asset found by several signals keeps the strongest (noisy-OR). A registrant organization that is a privacy proxy or placeholder is excluded, not scored, and a name match alone is never sufficient. The scored runtime scope-expansion decision and the classifier read the same catalog, so the lens, the engine and the model share one source of truth.

signals.title: Shared netblock registrant organization
signals.finds: A netblock whose RIR/WHOIS registration (IPNetRecord) names the same organization as its registrant as the target's.
signals.rationale: A Regional Internet Registry assigns an IP allocation to a specific organization and records it as the registrant of the inetnum/NetRange. When a netblock's registration names the target organization, the registry attributes that address space to it, which is direct evidence it belongs to the organization's footprint.
guards: A privacy or proxy registrant organization is never an anchor: it is shared by many unrelated allocations.
A matching organization name alone, with no shared registration record, is never sufficient.
counter_indications: A hosting or transit provider is the RIR registrant for address space it sub-allocates to many customers.
Legacy allocations can name a predecessor organization after an acquisition.

signals.title: Shared AS registrant organization
signals.finds: An autonomous system whose RIR/WHOIS registration (AutnumRecord) names the same organization as its registrant as the target's.
signals.rationale: An autonomous system number is registered to one operator, recorded as the registrant of the aut-num. When an AS registration names the target organization, the registry attributes that AS to it, direct evidence the AS is part of its network.
guards: A privacy or proxy registrant organization is never an anchor.
A matching organization name alone is never sufficient.
counter_indications: A parent or network operator can hold the AS registration for legally separate subsidiaries.
Upstream providers sometimes register AS numbers on behalf of customers.
